title: Etale target locality and permanence of affine space morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their fppf sheaves and small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. All indexing sets are small in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale chart from a quasi-compact scheme; a morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback over every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source. Quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, respectively the relative diagonal for a morphism, is quasi-compact. A morphism is affine if it is representable and its pullback over every affine scheme test has affine scheme source [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces. The morphism $f$ is affine if and only if there is a scheme $V$ and a representable surjective etale morphism $V\to Y$ such that $X\times_Y V\to V$ is an affine morphism of schemes. Affine morphisms are stable under arbitrary algebraic-space base change and composition; they are quasi-compact and separated (their representable diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]). If $Y$ is a scheme and $f$ is affine, then $X$ is a scheme, and if $Y$ is affine, $X$ is affine. If $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f$ is affine, then $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

proof.text: First establish the affine-test recognition needed throughout. Suppose a morphism $h:A\to B$ of spaces has affine scheme source after every affine scheme test of $B$. For any scheme $T\to B$, choose an affine open cover $(T_i)$ of $T$ and put $A_T=A\times_BT$. The subfunctors $A_T\times_TT_i$ are represented by affine schemes. Their inclusions are representable open immersions: on any scheme $Z\to A_T$, their pullbacks are the open subschemes $Z\times_TT_i$, which cover $Z$. The fppf sheaf $A_T$ is a Zariski sheaf, so [lem-pc-schemes-criterion] applies and represents $A_T$ by a scheme. Its map to $T$ is affine because the inverse image of each affine open of $T$ is affine. Thus $h$ is representable and affine. Conversely, an affine scheme morphism satisfies the affine-test condition: its base change is affine and an affine morphism over an affine scheme has affine source by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1),(2). In particular an affine space map to a scheme has scheme source, and its source is affine when the target is affine.

Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$, supplied by the definition of an algebraic space. If $f$ is affine, its base change to $V$ is affine by the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-four-property-fppf-descent]; Step 1 makes it an affine morphism of schemes. Conversely, suppose such an atlas has affine scheme pullback. This scheme pullback satisfies the space affine-test predicate by Step 1. The singleton $\{V\to Y\}$ is an fppf covering: it is jointly surjective and, on every etale scheme chart of $Y$, the pulled-back map is an etale scheme morphism, hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply the affine clause of [lem-sfb-space-four-property-fppf-descent]. It gives the affine-test predicate for $f$, and Step 1 supplies representability. This proves both implications without assuming $X$ or $Y$ schematic.

For any algebraic-space map $Y'\to Y$ and affine scheme $T\to Y'$, transitivity of sheaf fibre products identifies $(X\times_YY')\times_{Y'}T$ with $X\times_YT$, an affine scheme. Step 1 therefore makes $X\times_YY'\to Y'$ representable and affine. This is arbitrary base change, not only scheme base change.

Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ both be affine and let $T\to Z$ be an affine scheme test. Then $Y_T=Y\times_ZT$ is an affine scheme, and $X\times_ZT\simeq X\times_YY_T$ is an affine scheme by the affine-test condition for $f$. Step 1 supplies representability for $gf$, so $gf$ is affine. This proves composition directly from tests.

Use the scheme atlas $V\to Y$ from Step 2. The map $f_V:X_V\to V$ is an affine scheme morphism, hence is quasi-compact and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). These scheme properties give the space-level tests of [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local] for $f_V$: for an affine scheme $Z\to V$, the scheme $X_V\times_VZ$ is affine over the affine $Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1),(2), hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and its own quasi-compact atlas; and for a scheme $T\to X_V\times_VX_V$, the test $T\times_{X_V\times_VX_V}X_V\to T$ is the base change of the closed immersion $\Delta_{f_V}$, hence a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Apply [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local] to this singleton jointly surjective etale family. It follows that $f$ is quasi-compact and its representable diagonal $\Delta_f$ is a closed immersion. No quasi-compactness of $V$, or of $Y$, is required here.

We will use the equivalent quasi-compact-test formulation explicitly. If $h:A\to B$ has quasi-compact pullback source over every affine scheme test, let $C\to B$ have quasi-compact space source. The atlas/topological equivalence in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] and [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] give an affine scheme atlas $U\to C$. Now $A\times_BU$ is quasi-compact, so by the definition it has a quasi-compact scheme atlas $P\to A\times_BU$. The composite $P\to A\times_BC$ is surjective etale by base change and composition of atlases. Thus $A\times_BC$ is quasi-compact by the same definition. Conversely the formulation for all quasi-compact spaces includes affine schemes by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Consequently quasi-compactness is stable under base change and composition: for composable $h,k$ and quasi-compact $C\to\operatorname{target}(k)$, first $\operatorname{source}(k)\times C$ is quasi-compact and then its pullback under $h$ is quasi-compact. This is just successive application of the formulation proved above.

If $Y$ is quasi-compact, apply Step 6 to the quasi-compact $f$ of Step 5 with $C=Y$ and its identity map: $X$ is quasi-compact. For quasi-separatedness put $D=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. View $X$, $Y$ and $f$ as algebraic spaces and a morphism over $D$ by [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers](1),(2); by its clause (1) the fibre products over $Y$ are unchanged, and Steps 5 and 6, proved for an arbitrary base scheme, apply over $D$. The absolute diagonal factors as $X\xrightarrow{\Delta_f}X\times_YX\xrightarrow bX\times_DX$, where $b$ is the pullback of $\Delta_{Y/D}$ along $f\times f$. Since $Y$ is quasi-separated, $\Delta_{Y/D}$ is quasi-compact, hence so is $b$ by Step 6. Every affine scheme test of $\Delta_f$ is a closed immersion of schemes, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc](b). Its source is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](2), and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Thus $\Delta_f$ is quasi-compact by the affine-test definition. Step 6 makes the composite $\Delta_{X/D}$ quasi-compact, proving that $X$ is quasi-separated. The fibre products and this factorization are taken absolutely over $D$, not merely over the originally fixed scheme $S$.

lean.statement: theorem affine_locality_and_permanence {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) : (MapIsAffine f ↔ ∃ (V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y.obj.obj), IsEtale a ∧ IsSurjective a ∧ ∃ (U : Over S) (p : U ⟶ V) (q : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsPullback q (yoneda.map p) f.hom.hom a ∧ IsAffineHom p.left) ∧ (MapIsAffine f → IsRepresentable f.hom.hom ∧ (∀ (X' Y' : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (p : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ Y'), IsPullback p.hom f'.hom f.hom g.hom → MapIsAffine f') ∧ (∀ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : Y ⟶ Z), MapIsAffine g → MapIsAffine (f ≫ g)) ∧ IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap f.hom.hom ∧ IsSeparatedPresheafMap f.hom.hom ∧ (∀ (V : Over S), Nonempty (Y.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj V) → ∃ (U : Over S), Nonempty (X.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj U) ∧ (IsAffine V.left → IsAffine U.left)) ∧ ((∃ (V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y.obj.obj), CompactSpace V.left ∧ IsEtale a ∧ IsSurjective a) → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated Y → (∃ (U : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), CompactSpace U.left ∧ IsEtale a ∧ IsSurjective a) ∧ IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X))
